LESSON: MONEY

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade three
Subject: MATHEMATICAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: Measurement 2.4 Time (10 lessons) By the end of the sub strand, the learner shou
Topic 2.5: Money
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Money, part of Measurement 2.4 Time (10 lessons) By the end of the sub strand, the learner shou in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade three MATHEMATICAL ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How can money be represented in different denominations?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify Kenyan currency notes up to sh.1000,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Money in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. count money in different denominations up to sh.1000,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Money in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. add money involving different denominations up to a sh.1000,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Money in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Money in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

F. convert money into different denominations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Money in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Money together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Citizenship: learner counts Kenyan currency notes in different denominations up to sh. 1000.

● Digital literacy: learner uses digital devices to play games involving money.

49

Values:
● Patriotism: learner exhibits honesty as they sort out Kenyan currency notes according to their value up to sh.1000.

● Responsibility: learner engages in assigned roles and duties as they role play buying and selling in the classroom model

shop.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Financial literacy: learner role plays buying and selling items in the classroom model shop.

Sustainable consumption: learner uses locally available materials from the environment to model Kenyan currency.

Link to other learning areas:

The learner is able to relate the skills used in modelling the Kenyan currency denominations to modelling skills in Creative

Activities.

50
